whatThisIs: Count what is in your own VCF without uploading it: records, PASS calls, variant types, transitions and transversions, and one sample's zygosity. Large and bgzipped files are read a piece at a time.
whenToUse: Use this to check a VCF before using it: whether it is the file you think it is, how many calls passed the caller's filters, and whether its Ti/Tv and het/hom-alt ratios look like the kind of data it should be.
inputs: A .vcf, .vcf.gz or .vcf.bgz file and, if it has more than one sample, the sample to count. The file stays in the browser tab.
output: Record, PASS, reference-only and multiallelic counts; SNV, insertion, deletion and other ALT alleles; transitions, transversions and Ti/Tv; the sample's heterozygous, homozygous-alternate, reference and missing calls and het/hom-alt; counts per chromosome; the bytes read. No expected range is printed.
